newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso's popularity at all time low - report.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso's popularity at all time low - report.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's approval rating is at an all time low of 50 percent according to a soon to be published IBOPE poll, a newspaper reported on Tuesday.

O Estado de Sao Paulo quoted Carlos Augusto Montenegro, the head of the IBOPE polling institute, as saying a new poll carried out this month showed Cardoso's approval rating had dropped 20 points from 70 percent in March.
Despite the sharp drop, Montenegro said Cardoso's approval rating continued to be very good considering he was half way through his four-year term.
However he said the president's popularity would continue to drop if the government did not invest in "social actions" such as the improvement of health, water and drainage services.
"What the poll shows is that bringing down inflation will not solve everything," Montenegro was quoted as saying in a reference to the government's successful anti-inflation plan.

Montenegro said the president's popularity index was hardest hit by widespread discontent following the government's adjustment of the minimum wage, which is used as a salary parameter for millions of Brazilians.
On April 25 the government increased the minimum wage to 120 reais ($112) a month from a previous level of 112 reais ($104).
Montenegro also cited growing sympathy with the landless movement and popular disgust with a municipal bond scandal as factors behind the decline in Cardoso's approval rating.

He said the poll was completed before the eruption of a cash-for-vote scandal last week, in which congressmen were accused of allegedly accepting bribes in exchange for voting for a bill that would allow Cardoso to run for reelection.
Montenegro refused to say who had commissioned the poll and said the complete results would be published later this week.
